beats.text: Welcome to episode fourteen, our second and final exam workshop. We'll work through two longer practice questions on calorimetry and data evaluation, recap how to choose a method, and finish with a quick diagnostic on the most common traps. These are original practice questions written for this series, not official exam questions.

Two retrieval checks first. How many moles of hydrochloric acid are in twenty-five point zero millilitres of a zero point two zero zero mole per litre solution? And a heater runs at six point zero zero volts and one point five zero amps for two point zero zero minutes. How much electrical energy does it supply? Pause and answer.

For the acid, convert the volume to litres first: zero point two zero zero times zero point zero two five zero is zero point zero zero five zero zero moles. For the heater, convert the time to seconds: six point zero zero times one point five zero times one hundred and twenty is one thousand and eighty joules. Units first, then multiply.
